units.title: Making the Right Choices
units.intro: Grammar: a review of tenses, confusing verbs, and the present simple in newspaper headlines.

cards.title: Tense review
rule: **Present simple:** habits and facts (*Water **boils** at 100 °C*). **Present continuous:** now. **Past simple:** finished past. **Present perfect** (have/has + pp): past actions connected to now, with *ever, never, already, yet, just, recently, since, for*: *I **have recently finished** my exams.*
**Future perfect** (will have + pp): completed before a future time: *By June I **will have finished** Grade 10.*

examples.text: By 2030 we will have built many schools.

cards.title: Step-by-step
cards.problem: The official report on the regional economic development ________ by the committee before the deadline last night.

steps.text: The subject 'The official report' is inanimate and cannot perform the action of submitting.
The time-marker 'last night' indicates the Simple Past tense, requiring the past passive form ($$\text{was/were} + \text{V}_3$$).

cards.title: Step-by-step
cards.problem: A massive amount of money ________ currently ________ to fund the construction of the new school library.

steps.text: The subject is 'A massive amount of money' (singular and inanimate), requiring the passive voice.
The time-marker 'currently' indicates an action in progress, requiring the Present Progressive Passive ($$\text{is/are} + \text{being} + \text{V}_3$$).
Students often choose 'is raising' (Option A) because they confuse active and passive progressive forms.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The high school teacher ________ a beautiful traditional gift by the students on her graduation day.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
This is a double-object passive where the Indirect Object 'The high school teacher' is placed in the subject position: $$\text{IO} + \text{be} + \text{V}_3 + \text{DO}$$.

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Students often choose 'gave' (Option A) because they see a person as the subject and assume the active voice. However, the context shows she received the gift, requiring the passive form 'was given' (Option B).

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
እቲ መምህር ባዕሉ ህያብ ኣይሃበን፤ বልኩስ ካብ ተመሃሮ ህያብ ተዋሂብዎ (received)። እዚ ዓይነት መዋቕር ድርብ ተቐባሊ ዘለዎ ግሲ (double-object passive) ኮይኑ፡ 'was given' (Option B - ተዋሂቡ) ቅኑዕ መልሲ ይኸውን። 'gave' እንተይልና እቲ መምህር ባዕሉ ንተመሃሮ ህያብ ሂብዎም ማለት ምኾነ።

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The national examination papers ________ by next Friday afternoon, according to the official schedule.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The inanimate subject 'examination papers' requires the passive voice. The time-marker 'by next Friday' indicates a future point of completion, requiring the Future Perfect Passive ($$\text{will have been} + \text{V}_3$$).

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Students often see 'next Friday' and choose active 'will print' (Option A) or active future perfect 'will have printed' (Option D). Because papers cannot print themselves, the passive 'will have been printed' (Option B) is correct.

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
'By next Friday' (ክሳብ ዝመጽእ ዓርቢ) ዝብል ሓረግ መጻኢ ፍጹም እዋን (Future Perfect) ከም ዘድልየና የረድኣና። እቲ ዋና ባእታ 'examination papers' (መፈተኒ ወረቐት) ህይወት ኣልቦ ስለ ዝኾነ ድማ እቲ ምሉእ ሓሳብ ኣብ Future Perfect Passive 'will have been printed' (Option B - ተሓቲሙ ክውዳእ እዩ) ክስራዕ ኣለዎ።

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Examination papers are collected by an invigilator at the end of the exam. (Choose the correct active form)

options.A: Examination papers collected by the invigilator at the end of the exam.
options.B: An invigilator collected examination papers at the end of the exam.
options.C: At the end of the exam, examination papers were collected by the invigilator.
options.D: Examination papers are collected by the invigilator at the end of the exam.
options.E: An invigilator collects examination papers at the end of the exam.

cards.why:
**Step 1:** The passive sentence is in the **Present Simple** ("are collected").
**Step 2:** The active form must be in the Present Simple. The agent is "an invigilator" (singular).
**Step 3:** "An invigilator collects" is the correct active form.

cards.title: Headlines in the present simple
rule: Newspaper headlines use the **present simple** for recent past events and leave out small words (*a, the, is*): ***Students Win** National Prize* = Students have won a national prize. A **to-infinitive** shows the future: ***Minister To Open** New School*. A past participle alone shows the passive: ***Bridge Opened** In Keren*.

examples.text: Headline: Bridge Opened In Keren (= a bridge has been opened)

cards.title: Memory tip
body: **Yesterday / ago → past simple. Since / for / yet → present perfect. By + future → will have done.**

cards.title: Unit summary
body: Choose tenses by their signal words: habits/facts (present simple), now (continuous), finished past (past simple), past linked to now (present perfect), finished before a future time (future perfect). Headlines use the present simple for recent events and to + verb for the future.

cards.title: Expand a headline into a full sentence
cards.problem: Write the headline "LOCAL GIRL WINS NATIONAL ESSAY PRIZE" as a full news sentence.

steps.text: **Step 1: Find the parts.** Subject: LOCAL GIRL; verb: WINS; object: NATIONAL ESSAY PRIZE.
**Step 2: Restore the time.** Headlines use the present simple for a recent past event, so "wins" means "has won" (or "won").
**Step 3: Restore the missing words.** Add the articles headlines leave out: "A local girl ... the national essay prize".
**Step 4: Write the sentence.** A local girl has won the national essay prize.
**Check:** "to + verb" in a headline would mean future (GIRL TO RECEIVE PRIZE = a girl is going to receive a prize).

cards.answer: A local girl has won the national essay prize.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: I_____ reading this book by the end of 2016.
cards.why: The phrase 'by the end of' is a time marker for the Future Perfect tense ($$ will + have + V3 $$). It indicates that an action will be completed at some point in the future before another event.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: What does the headline "NEW HOSPITAL TO OPEN IN BARENTU" mean?

options.A: A new hospital opened in Barentu last year.
options.B: A new hospital is going to open in Barentu.
options.D: A new hospital is closing in Barentu.

cards.why:
**Step 1:** "to + verb" in a headline refers to the future.

**Step 2:** So "TO OPEN" means "is going to open".

**Step 3:** The article "A" is omitted, as is usual in headlines.

**Tip:** Match the tense to the time: habits (present simple), now (present continuous), finished past (past simple), past to now (present perfect). Headlines use the present simple for past events and drop articles and "be".

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Which headline means "Heavy rain has caused floods in Gash-Barka"?

options.A: HEAVY RAIN CAUSES FLOODS IN GASH-BARKA
options.B: HEAVY RAIN CAUSING FLOODS WILL BE
options.D: HEAVY RAIN TO CAUSE FLOODS IN GASH-BARKA

cards.why:
**Step 1:** A recent past event is reported in the present simple in headlines.

**Step 2:** "CAUSES" = has caused.

**Step 3:** "TO CAUSE" would mean future, and the last option reverses the meaning.

**Tip:** Match the tense to the time: habits (present simple), now (present continuous), finished past (past simple), past to now (present perfect). Headlines use the present simple for past events and drop articles and "be".
